title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'équation des lacets' notes, i.e. Grothendieck's own parametrisation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group. pi = pi_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. It carries the S_3 symmetries, with rho of order 3 and sigma_infty of order 2. A tilde means the group enlarged by an extra involution tau_infty. M^{!~}_{0,3} is a set of automorphisms u (of pi extended by these finite symmetries) that send each finite generator to a conjugate of itself.

On the previous page, u is coded by (g,h,f). Here g and h satisfy the 'cocycle' relations (25), which are of the form g·rho(g)·rho^2(g)=1 and h·sigma_infty(h)=1. The single loop relation (29) links them to f. Grothendieck then writes g = alpha_0 rho(alpha_0)^{-1} and h = beta_0 sigma_infty(beta_0)^{-1}: the cocycles become coboundaries. That is legitimate because every order-3 (resp. order-2) element in the right coset is conjugate to rho (resp. sigma_infty) in the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) or PGL_2(Z).

On this page:
(i) The coboundary parametrisation makes (25) automatic. Only the loop relation (34) remains. The relations (23) become u(sigma_infty) = int(beta_0)(sigma_infty) and u(rho) = int(alpha_0)(rho). So u is determined by which conjugates of the two finite subgroups it hits, i.e. by its values on the generators of the free product Z/2 * Z/3.
(ii) In (34), alpha_0, beta_0 and f only enter through f·alpha_0 and f·beta_0. Setting alpha = f·alpha_0 and beta = f·beta_0, u is coded by triples (alpha, beta, f). These are taken modulo the simultaneous left translation (alpha, beta, f) -> (l_0^n alpha, l_0^n beta, l_0^n f), with n in Z^. They are subject to the boxed 'loop relation in alpha, beta' (37): alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} = (beta sigma_infty(beta)^{-1}) · l_1^nu, in which f no longer appears.
(iii) Inverse formulas: alpha_0 = f^{-1} alpha and beta_0 = f^{-1} beta. Then g = f^{-1} xi rho(f) and h = f^{-1} eta sigma_infty(f), with xi = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} and eta = beta sigma_infty(beta)^{-1}.

On the next page this gives u = int(f^{-1}) u_{alpha,beta} and the 'commutation relation' xi = eta l_1^nu. There xi and eta are a Z/3-cocycle and a Z/2-cocycle respectively.

Overall, the page reformulates the GT-type defining equations as nonabelian-cohomology (coboundary) data. It separates an inner-automorphism part f from the essential data (alpha, beta). The margin notes that the real parameters, i.e. the indeterminacy (alpha, beta) -> (l_0^n alpha, l_0^n beta), remain to be examined.
errors: (40): the middle expression f^{-1}(beta sigma_infty(beta)^{-1}) omits the factor sigma_infty(f) on the right. The correct form is f^{-1}(beta sigma_infty(beta)^{-1}) sigma_infty(f), and the final expression f^{-1} eta sigma_infty(f) is correct. This is a slip of the pen.
The label (35) is used twice, once for the formulas u(sigma_infty)=..., u(rho)=... and once for alpha = f alpha_0, beta = f beta_0.
The claim that xi, eta lie in pi_{0,3}^ while alpha may lie in the enlarged group (with tau_infty) needs tau_infty to commute with rho modulo pi. This is not verified on the page.

The 'bijective correspondence' (g,h) <-> (alpha_0, beta_0) quoted from the previous page tacitly uses two facts. First, the centraliser of rho (resp. sigma_infty) in the relevant group is trivial modulo the finite group. Second, all order-3/order-2 elements in the coset are conjugate to rho/sigma_infty. Both are true for profinite Z/2*Z/3 but are not argued here.

ideas.what: Trivialising the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of the GT-type equations by writing the cocycles g, h as coboundaries alpha_0 rho(alpha_0)^{-1}, beta_0 sigma(beta_0)^{-1}. Equivalently, u sends the finite generators rho and sigma_infty to conjugates.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1 of finite cyclic groups acting on pi_{0,3}^; description of GT via automorphisms of profinite PSL_2(Z)/PGL_2(Z) preserving the conjugacy classes of torsion; cohomological interpretation of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps (GT and automorphisms of braid groups / cohomological interpretation of GT, 1990s); Drinfeld 1990 for GT itself
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and Gal acting on pi_{0,3}. This explicit reparametrisation is in the unpublished 'Longue Marche' sequel notes.

ideas.what: Elimination of the inner-automorphism parameter f: setting alpha = f alpha_0 and beta = f beta_0 gives a loop relation alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} = beta sigma(beta)^{-1} l_1^nu involving only (alpha, beta), with u = int(f^{-1}) u_{alpha,beta}.
ideas.modern_name: Separation of an automorphism into its outer class plus an inner part; a normal form of the GT equations modulo inner automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Drinfeld/Ihara/Lochak–Schneps treatments of GT as a subgroup of Out

ideas.what: The indeterminacy by simultaneous left multiplication by l_0^n (n in Z^), the centraliser of l_0, and the question of the 'true parameters'.
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser/centraliser ambiguity in parametrising GT elements

missed.claim: The margin flags that the true parameter space for (alpha, beta) modulo l_0^n, with the loop relation (37) and the unknown exponent nu, has yet to be determined. This would give a description of M^{!~}_{0,3} purely in terms of pairs of conjugating elements for the order-2 and order-3 generators. It is close to, but not obviously identical with, the Lochak–Schneps cocycle description.
missed.quote: il reste à examiner quels sont les vrais paramètres
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It shows Grothendieck independently reaching (pre-Drinfeld) the coboundary/conjugacy reformulation of the GT relations that Lochak–Schneps later published. A specialist would find the (alpha, beta) normal form familiar rather than new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, routine-but-substantive reparametrisation of the GT-type equations by coboundaries. It anticipates the known Lochak–Schneps-style reformulation (GT as automorphisms sending torsion generators of profinite PSL_2(Z) to conjugates). That is interesting as priority history but contains no result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The underlined parenthetical after the 'modulo' line, transcribed '(inconnu[?] pour alpha, beta, f)', reads '(simultanément pour alpha, beta, f)', i.e. the l_0^n translation is applied simultaneously.

(40) in the image indeed reads h = beta_0 sigma_infty(beta_0)^{-1} = f^{-1}(beta sigma_infty(beta)^{-1}) = f^{-1} eta sigma_infty(f). The missing sigma_infty(f) is Grothendieck's slip, not a transcription error.
In (39) Grothendieck crossed out something under alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} before rho(f).

Margin (oblique) plausibly reads: 'Une discussion des triples ... de l'indétermination des couples (alpha, beta) -> (l_0^n alpha, l_0^n beta) (n in Z^) mais il reste à examiner quels sont les vrais paramètres'. Uncertain.
